summary: Audit of evidence_blobs.store_blob() chmod ordering against the security finding. The current code applies Path(tmp_name).chmod(0o600) BEFORE os.replace(tmp_name, path) (lines 120-121 of src/mac/evidence_blobs.py), which correctly eliminates the TOCTOU window. The original finding (chmod after rename) no longer applies. All 16 tests in test_evidence_blobs.py pass, including test_store_blob_sets_mode_0600. No code change required.

audit_findings.finding_description: Security audit of evidence_blobs.store_blob() chmod-0600 ordering relative to os.replace() atomic rename.
audit_findings.original_concern: The finding alleged that chmod(0o600) was called AFTER the atomic os.replace() rename rather than before it (as done correctly in bitwarden.py). If true, this would create a brief TOCTOU window during which the final blob file would be world-readable under a permissive umask.
audit_findings.current_code_order: CORRECT: chmod is applied to the temp file path BEFORE the atomic rename. Line 120 (Path(tmp_name).chmod(0o600)) precedes line 121 (os.replace(tmp_name, path)).
audit_findings.permission_window_race: NONE: The temp file is chmoded to 0600 while it still has the tmp_name path. The os.replace() then atomically promotes the already-restricted file to the final path. There is no window during which the final path exists with permissive permissions.
audit_findings.tmpfile_default_permissions: tempfile.mkstemp() on Linux already creates files with mode 0600 (observed: 0o100600) regardless of umask, because it passes O_CREAT|O_EXCL with 0600 internally. However, the explicit chmod is still correct practice for portability and defense-in-depth, and matches the bitwarden.py pattern.
audit_findings.dedup_path_protection: The post-rename path.chmod(0o600) at line 129 (inside try/except OSError) serves as defense-in-depth for the pre-existing-file dedup path, where the blob already exists and no rename occurs. This path is safe because the file was written by a previous correct invocation.
audit_findings.bitwarden_comparison: bitwarden.py (src/mac/_hermes/agent/secret_sources/bitwarden.py, line 160): os.chmod(tmp, 0o600) is called before os.replace(tmp, path) at line 161 — identical pattern to the current evidence_blobs.py implementation.
audit_findings.severity: NONE — the original finding does not apply to the current code. The code is safe-as-is.
audit_findings.verdict: SAFE. No code changes required. The security model is correctly implemented: (1) mkstemp creates a 0600 temp file, (2) content is written, (3) chmod 0600 is applied to the temp path before rename, (4) os.replace atomically renames the already-restricted file, (5) a defense-in-depth post-rename chmod covers the dedup path.
